concepts.title: Origins and Three Broad Branches of Ayurveda

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Origins and Three Broad Branches of Ayurveda' refers to.
questions.a: An ancient Indian medical tradition stemming from Vedic thought that comprehensively studies the health and diseases of human beings, animals, and plant life under uniform natural principles.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Origins and Three Broad Branches of Ayurveda'.
questions.a: Universal life science applying common physical and physiological principles across all biological kingdoms.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Origins and Three Broad Branches of Ayurveda', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: Ayurveda = Manushya Ayurveda + Mrga Ayurveda + Vrksa Ayurveda

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Classical Literature of Ayurveda' refers to.
questions.a: The extensive body of codified ancient treatises documenting medical theories, surgical techniques, pediatrics, and botanical knowledge across centuries.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Classical Literature of Ayurveda'.
questions.a: Centuries of systematic clinical observations and medical therapies preserved in rigorous Sanskrit compilations.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Classical Literature of Ayurveda', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: Major texts = Caraka Samhita + Susruta Samhita + Astanga Hrdaya

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Astanga Ayurveda: Eight Clinical Specialties' refers to.
questions.a: The eightfold branch organization of clinical Ayurvedic medicine spanning general medicine, surgery, head and neck diseases, pediatrics, toxicology, psychiatry, rejuvenation, and virility.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Astanga Ayurveda: Eight Clinical Specialties'.
questions.a: Comprehensive division of clinical medicine into eight distinct specialized therapeutic fields.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Astanga Ayurveda: Eight Clinical Specialties', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: Astanga = Kaya + Shalya + Shalakya + Kaumarabhrtya + Agada + Bhoota Vidya + Rasayana + Vajikarana

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Philosophical Foundations: Role of Darsanas' refers to.
questions.a: The conceptual integration of classical Indian philosophical systems into Ayurveda to formulate theories of matter, cognition, physical elements, and logic.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Philosophical Foundations: Role of Darsanas'.
questions.a: Ayurveda builds its scientific and observational methods upon the fundamental worldviews of Indian philosophical schools.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Philosophical Foundations: Role of Darsanas', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: Ayurvedic Framework = Vaisesika + Nyaya + Samkhya + Yoga + Mimamsa + Vedanta

concepts.title: Four Interconnected Domains of the Human System

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Four Interconnected Domains of the Human System' refers to.
questions.a: The multi-tiered conception of the individual human being consisting of interconnected structural, physiological, psychological, and conscious domains.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Four Interconnected Domains of the Human System'.
questions.a: The human entity is a seamless continuum linking physical body networks with mental properties and layers of awareness.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Four Interconnected Domains of the Human System', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: Human System = Structural (Srotas) + Physiological (Tridosha) + Psychological (Manasikadosha) + Consciousness (Pancakosa)

concepts.title: Tridosha Theory and the Twenty Properties (Vimsatiguna)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Tridosha Theory and the Twenty Properties (Vimsatiguna)' refers to.
questions.a: The foundational tripartite functional model of physiology governing motion (Vata), biochemical transformation (Pitta), and structural stability (Kapha), characterized by ten opposing property pairs.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Tridosha Theory and the Twenty Properties (Vimsatiguna)'.
questions.a: Health corresponds to homeostatic dynamic balance of Vata, Pitta, and Kapha, while disease represents a perturbation in this network.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Tridosha Theory and the Twenty Properties (Vimsatiguna)', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: Tridosha = Vata (movement) + Pitta (metabolism) + Kapha (growth/support)

concepts.title: Biological Rhythms: Daily and Seasonal Regimens

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Biological Rhythms: Daily and Seasonal Regimens' refers to.
questions.a: Preventive and promotive lifestyle protocols synchronized with daily 24-hour cycles (Dinacarya) and annual seasonal variations (Rtucarya) to sustain doshic balance.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Biological Rhythms: Daily and Seasonal Regimens'.
questions.a: Aligning personal activities and food habits with nature's cyclic changes prevents seasonal dosha fluctuations and illness.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Biological Rhythms: Daily and Seasonal Regimens', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: Health Maintenance = Dinacarya (Circadian) + Rtucarya (Circa-annual)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Dietetics, Nutrition, and Six Tastes (Sadrata)' refers to.
questions.a: The dietary science that categorizes food ingredients by their sensory tastes, thermal impacts, digestibility, and capacity to balance or aggravate doshas.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Dietetics, Nutrition, and Six Tastes (Sadrata)'.
questions.a: A balanced meal contains all six tastes processed to balance individual constitutional needs and seasonal demands.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Dietetics, Nutrition, and Six Tastes (Sadrata)', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: Six Rasas = Madhura (sweet) + Amla (sour) + Lavana (salty) + Katu (pungent) + Tikta (bitter) + Kasaya (astringent)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Ayurvedic Pharmacology: Dravyaguna Vijnana' refers to.
questions.a: The pharmacological discipline analyzing medicinal materials through taste (rasa), biophysical properties (guna), potency (virya), and multi-compound synergy.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Ayurvedic Pharmacology: Dravyaguna Vijnana'.
questions.a: Herbal preparations extract whole active compound complexes utilizing water, oil, ghee, and alcohol bases for multi-target therapy.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Ayurvedic Pharmacology: Dravyaguna Vijnana', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: Pharmacological Action = Rasa + Guna + Virya + Vipaka + Prabhava

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Convergence with Modern Biomedical Concepts' refers to.
questions.a: The conceptual convergence between ancient Ayurvedic principles and modern biomedical frontiers including systems biology, pharmacogenomics, circadian chronobiology, and sustainable ecology.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Convergence with Modern Biomedical Concepts'.
questions.a: Modern medical research increasingly validates holistic, individualized, and chronobiological principles central to Ayurveda.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Convergence with Modern Biomedical Concepts', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: Modern Convergence = Systems Biology + Prakrti-based Personalized Medicine + Circadian Clocks + Ecological Health
